problem:
$$
P=[\begin{aligned}5 & 2 & -6 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 7 \\ 0 & -3 & -4 & 9 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Consider the matrix $P$ given above. Which of the following statements are true?

- $\lambda =0$ is an eigenvalue of $P$
- $\lambda =-4$ is an eigenvalue of $P$
- The eigenvalue $\lambda =2$ has algebraic multiplicity $2$

examples.knowledge_point: Calculating the Eigenvalues of a 4x4 Matrix Containing a Block of Zeros
examples.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14069304/assets/2379f9f0cec3f257da5a4c0695f114d0bc7f3b4c914edabfd690ff94705faceb.png)

Consider the matrix $P$ given above. Which of the following statements are true?

- $\lambda=4$ is an eigenvalue of $P$

- $\lambda=-1$ is an eigenvalue of $P$

- The eigenvalue $\lambda=6$ has algebraic multiplicity $2$
examples.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\, P-\lambda I \mathbin{:}$
﻿﻿﻿![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14069304/assets/8ee9ef991440e5641d6a458c0384382b54eb3d8504856b942fc33cf24b0b85e9.png)

The characteristic equation is $\det(P-\lambda I) = 0.$ 

Notice that we can expand the $4 \times 4$ determinant across the $1$st column, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(P-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}3-\lambda  & 0 & -8 & -2 \\ 0 & -1-\lambda  & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 4-\lambda  & 0 \\ 0 & 7 & -3 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (3-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}-1-\lambda  & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & 4-\lambda  & 0 \\ 7 & -3 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, expanding the $3 \times 3$ determinant across the $2$nd row, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}(3-\lambda )\cdot (4-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}-1-\lambda  & 5 \\ 7 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (3-\lambda )(4-\lambda )((-1-\lambda )(1-\lambda )-35) & =0 \\ (3-\lambda )(4-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-36) & =0 \\ (\lambda -3)(\lambda -4)(\lambda -6)(\lambda +6) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

So, the eigenvalues of $P$ are $\lambda=3,$ $\lambda=4,$ $\lambda=6,$ and $\lambda=-6$ (all with algebraic multiplicity $1$).

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."

feedback.problem:
Find the characteristic equation of the matrix 
$A=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 2 & -1 \\ 5 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,A-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
A-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}-3-\lambda  & 2 & -1 \\ 5 & 2-\lambda  & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

The characteristic equation is $det(A-\lambda I)=0.$ 

Expanding the determinant across the $3$rd row, we obtain the following:  

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-3-\lambda  & 2 & -1 \\ 5 & 2-\lambda  & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}-3-\lambda  & 2 \\ 5 & 2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )((-3-\lambda )(2-\lambda )-2\cdot 5) & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}+\lambda -16) & =0\end{aligned}
$$
